hook.text: A test is 99% accurate. You test positive. Most people think there's a 99% chance you're sick. Wrong.

buildup.text: If the disease affects 1 in 10,000 people, most positives are false. The base rate changes everything.

discovery.text: Base rate neglect means ignoring how common something is and focusing only on the specific evidence.

twist.text: Bayes' theorem fixes this by combining the test result with the prior probability. Few people use it intuitively.

climax.text: In courts, juries convict on vivid evidence while ignoring that the crime type is extremely rare.

punchline.text: How common it is matters more than how well it fits.

quiz.question: What is base rate neglect?
options: Ignoring how common something is when judging probability
